programme.subtitle: Monitor one Amazon Linux 2023 EC2 instance with metrics, logs, alarms, notifications, dashboards, and troubleshooting evidence
programme.description: This self-paced lab creates a small isolated EC2 monitoring environment in eu-west-2. You create a dedicated IAM training user, a dedicated VPC, a Systems Manager-managed Amazon Linux 2023 instance, the unified CloudWatch Agent, custom metrics, CloudWatch Logs metric filters, SNS notifications, static and anomaly-detection alarms, a composite alarm, a dashboard, and Logs Insights queries. The final phase removes only the resources created by this Follow Along.
programme.learningOutcome: Create and interpret CloudWatch metrics, logs, alarms, dashboards, agent telemetry, EC2 status checks, and EBS monitoring; distinguish CloudWatch from EventBridge, CloudTrail, and AWS Config; and select appropriate monitoring patterns for SAA-C03 scenarios.

tasks.title: Create the dedicated non-root training user
tasks.goal: Create fa-cloudwatch-lab-user before creating any lab infrastructure.
tasks.whyItMatters: The AWS account root user has unrestricted access. AWS recommends using root only for the small set of account-only tasks, protecting it with MFA, and never creating root access keys. The dedicated user makes the lab activity identifiable and removable.

consoleSteps.title: Create the training user
consoleSteps.instruction: Open the AWS Management Console as an administrator-capable identity.

instructions.text: Open the AWS Management Console as an administrator-capable identity.
Select Provide user access to the AWS Management Console.
Select I want to create an IAM user.
Select Users must create a new password at next sign-in.
Record the Console sign-in URL shown in the Summary section as [IAM_SIGN_IN_URL].

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The IAM Users list contains fa-cloudwatch-lab-user.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not create or use root access keys. Store the user password securely and do not place it in notes, source code, screenshots, or commands.

cliSteps.command: aws iam create-user --user-name fa-cloudwatch-lab-user --profile <ADMIN_PROFILE>
cliSteps.explanation: Run this as an existing administrator. IAM is global, so this command intentionally does not use --region. Replace <ADMIN_PROFILE> with the local administrator profile that existed before this lab.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains UserName fa-cloudwatch-lab-user.
cliSteps.warning: Do not run this command with root access keys.

verification.title: Verify the dedicated identity exists
verification.instruction: In IAM > Users, select fa-cloudwatch-lab-user.
verification.expectedResult: The user details page identifies User name as fa-cloudwatch-lab-user.

tasks.title: Create and attach the least-privilege training policy
tasks.goal: Create fa-cloudwatch-lab-policy and attach it only to the training user.
tasks.whyItMatters: The learner needs permissions to create only this lab's monitoring, notification, EC2, VPC, Systems Manager, and IAM resources. Creation and Describe APIs often require Resource * because an AWS resource does not exist yet or because the API does not support resource-level permissions. The instance receives a separate, narrower role.

consoleSteps.title: Create the customer-managed training policy

instructions.text: Replace the policy editor content with the displayed policy JSON.
Replace <ACCOUNT_ID> with the 12-digit account ID shown in the upper-right AWS Console account menu.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: fa-cloudwatch-lab-policy is attached to fa-cloudwatch-lab-user.
consoleSteps.warning: This is a deliberately bounded training policy, not a production authorization design. Do not attach it to any other identity.

cliSteps.command: aws iam create-policy --policy-name fa-cloudwatch-lab-policy --policy-document file://fa-cloudwatch-lab-policy.json --profile <ADMIN_PROFILE>
cliSteps.explanation: First save the exact JSON shown in this task as fa-cloudwatch-lab-policy.json and replace <ACCOUNT_ID>. This creates the customer-managed policy.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response includes an Arn ending in policy/fa-cloudwatch-lab-policy.
cliSteps.warning: IAM is global; omit --region.

cliSteps.command: aws iam attach-user-policy --user-name fa-cloudwatch-lab-user --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::<ACCOUNT_ID>:policy/fa-cloudwatch-lab-policy --profile <ADMIN_PROFILE>
cliSteps.explanation: Replace <ACCOUNT_ID> with the account ID used in the policy document. This attaches the policy to only the training user.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command completes without output.
cliSteps.warning: IAM permission changes can take a short time to propagate.

verification.title: Verify the intended attachment
verification.instruction: Open IAM > Users > fa-cloudwatch-lab-user > Permissions.
verification.expectedResult: The Permissions policies table lists fa-cloudwatch-lab-policy.

verification.title: Verify the instance-role separation
verification.instruction: Inspect the training-policy JSON.
verification.expectedResult: The training user can pass only fa-cloudwatch-instance-role to EC2; the CloudWatch Agent permissions are not attached to the human user as an AWS managed agent policy.

tasks.title: Create safe CLI access and verify the training identity
tasks.goal: Create one temporary IAM access key for the training user, configure the named fa-cloudwatch-lab profile for eu-west-2, and verify the caller.
tasks.whyItMatters: A named profile reduces accidental use of another account or Region. An access key secret is shown once; never place it in this lab, a command history, or a screenshot.

consoleSteps.title: Create the training access key

instructions.text: In Access keys, choose Create access key.
Record the Access key ID displayed on this page as [TRAINING_ACCESS_KEY_ID].
Store the file in a secure local location.
Delete the downloaded file after configuring the CLI.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The user has one active access key and its ID is recorded as [TRAINING_ACCESS_KEY_ID].
consoleSteps.warning: The secret access key is displayed only once. Do not paste it into this Follow Along, a browser page, a shell history, source code, or screenshots.

cliSteps.command: aws configure --profile fa-cloudwatch-lab
cliSteps.explanation: At the prompts, enter the newly created access key ID, its secret access key, eu-west-2 as Default region name, and json as Default output format. The credentials are entered locally and are not displayed by this Follow Along.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The local shared AWS CLI configuration contains profile fa-cloudwatch-lab.
cliSteps.warning: This interactive command writes credentials to the local AWS shared credentials file.

cliSteps.command: aws sts get-caller-identity --profile fa-cloudwatch-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: This proves which account and principal the named profile uses.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The Arn identifies user/fa-cloudwatch-lab-user.
cliSteps.warning: Stop and correct the profile if the Arn identifies root or another user.

verification.title: Verify non-root console use
verification.instruction: Sign out and sign in through [IAM_SIGN_IN_URL] as fa-cloudwatch-lab-user.
verification.expectedResult: The upper-right Console menu identifies fa-cloudwatch-lab-user.

verification.title: Verify CLI identity
verification.instruction: Inspect the Arn returned by get-caller-identity.
verification.expectedResult: The Arn ends with user/fa-cloudwatch-lab-user.

tasks.title: Create the isolated VPC, public subnet, route, and instance security group
tasks.goal: Create the minimum internet-egress-only networking required for Systems Manager and package installation.
tasks.whyItMatters: The instance needs outbound connectivity to Systems Manager and package repositories. The security group intentionally has no inbound rules, so Session Manager replaces SSH.

consoleSteps.title: Create the VPC and subnet

instructions.text: Enter 10.60.0.0/24 in IPv4 subnet CIDR block.
Select Enable auto-assign public IPv4 address.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: fa-cloudwatch-vpc and fa-cloudwatch-public-a exist, and the subnet assigns public IPv4 addresses.
consoleSteps.warning: Use only this new VPC. Do not modify a default or shared VPC.

consoleSteps.title: Create internet routing and the no-ingress security group

instructions.text: Enter fa-cloudwatch-instance-sg in Security group name.
Enter No inbound access; Session Manager only in Description.
Record the displayed Security group ID as [INSTANCE_SG_ID].

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The subnet has a default route to the new internet gateway, and the instance security group has zero inbound rules.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not add SSH, HTTP, HTTPS, or any other inbound rule.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-vpc --cidr-block 10.60.0.0/16 --tag-specifications ResourceType=vpc,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-cloudwatch-vpc}] --profile fa-cloudwatch-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record VpcId from the Vpc object as [VPC_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: A VPC with CIDR 10.60.0.0/16 is returned.
cliSteps.warning: Use only [VPC_ID] returned by this command in later VPC commands.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 modify-vpc-attribute --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --enable-dns-support {"Value":true} --profile fa-cloudwatch-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Enable DNS resolution in the lab VPC.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command completes without output.
cliSteps.warning: Replace [VPC_ID] with the earlier VpcId.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 modify-vpc-attribute --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --enable-dns-hostnames {"Value":true} --profile fa-cloudwatch-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Enable DNS hostnames for the lab VPC.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command completes without output.
cliSteps.warning: Replace [VPC_ID] with the earlier VpcId.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-subnet --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --availability-zone eu-west-2a --cidr-block 10.60.0.0/24 --tag-specifications ResourceType=subnet,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-cloudwatch-public-a}] --profile fa-cloudwatch-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record SubnetId as [SUBNET_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The public subnet is returned.
cliSteps.warning: If eu-west-2a is unavailable to the account, use the Console route and select an available eu-west-2 Availability Zone.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 modify-subnet-attribute --subnet-id [SUBNET_ID] --map-public-ip-on-launch --profile fa-cloudwatch-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Configure the lab subnet to assign a public IPv4 address at launch.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command completes without output.
cliSteps.warning: The security group still has no inbound rules.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-internet-gateway --tag-specifications ResourceType=internet-gateway,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-cloudwatch-igw}] --profile fa-cloudwatch-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record InternetGatewayId as [IGW_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The new internet gateway is returned.
cliSteps.warning: Attach it only to [VPC_ID].

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 attach-internet-gateway --internet-gateway-id [IGW_ID] --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --profile fa-cloudwatch-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Attach the lab internet gateway to the lab VPC.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command completes without output.
cliSteps.warning: Replace both identifiers with resources created in this task.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-route-table --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --tag-specifications ResourceType=route-table,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-cloudwatch-public-rt}] --profile fa-cloudwatch-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record RouteTableId as [ROUTE_TABLE_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The route table is returned.
cliSteps.warning: Do not use the VPC main route table.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id [ROUTE_TABLE_ID] --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --gateway-id [IGW_ID] --profile fa-cloudwatch-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Create the IPv4 default route through the new internet gateway.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response identifies the new active route.
cliSteps.warning: Do not add an inbound security-group rule as part of this networking setup.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 associate-route-table --route-table-id [ROUTE_TABLE_ID] --subnet-id [SUBNET_ID] --profile fa-cloudwatch-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record AssociationId as [ROUTE_ASSOCIATION_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The association response includes AssociationId.
cliSteps.warning: This association must be removed before deleting the route table.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-security-group --group-name fa-cloudwatch-instance-sg --description "No inbound access; Session Manager only" --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --profile fa-cloudwatch-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record GroupId as [INSTANCE_SG_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The security group is returned with no inbound permissions.
cliSteps.warning: Do not run authorize-security-group-ingress for this lab.

verification.title: Verify isolated access
verification.instruction: Inspect fa-cloudwatch-instance-sg > Inbound rules.
verification.expectedResult: The inbound rules table is empty.

verification.title: Verify route placement
verification.instruction: Inspect fa-cloudwatch-public-rt > Routes and Subnet associations.
verification.expectedResult: 0.0.0.0/0 targets fa-cloudwatch-igw and fa-cloudwatch-public-a is explicitly associated.

tasks.title: Create the EC2 Systems Manager and CloudWatch Agent role
tasks.feature: IAM role for managed node telemetry
tasks.goal: Create an EC2 role, attach Systems Manager and CloudWatch Agent managed policies, and create the instance profile before launching EC2.
tasks.whyItMatters: The instance role supplies temporary credentials to the SSM Agent and CloudWatch Agent. This is safer than placing access keys on an instance.

consoleSteps.title: Create the EC2 role and instance profile

instructions.text: Confirm fa-cloudwatch-instance-role appears as an available profile.

jsonBlocks.title: EC2 trust policy used by the CLI route

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The EC2 role has both required AWS managed policies and is available as an EC2 instance profile.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not attach CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy to the human training user. It belongs on the EC2 role.

cliSteps.command: aws iam create-role --role-name fa-cloudwatch-instance-role --assume-role-policy-document file://fa-cloudwatch-ec2-trust-policy.json --profile fa-cloudwatch-lab
cliSteps.explanation: Save the displayed trust-policy JSON as fa-cloudwatch-ec2-trust-policy.json before running this command.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response includes RoleName fa-cloudwatch-instance-role.
cliSteps.warning: IAM is global; omit --region.

cliSteps.command: aws iam attach-role-policy --role-name fa-cloudwatch-instance-role --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore --profile fa-cloudwatch-lab
cliSteps.explanation: Allow the node to be managed with Systems Manager Session Manager.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command completes without output.
cliSteps.warning: IAM is global; omit --region.

cliSteps.command: aws iam attach-role-policy --role-name fa-cloudwatch-instance-role --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy --profile fa-cloudwatch-lab
cliSteps.explanation: Allow the CloudWatch Agent to publish metrics and logs from the instance.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command completes without output.
cliSteps.warning: IAM is global; omit --region.

cliSteps.command: aws iam create-instance-profile --instance-profile-name fa-cloudwatch-instance-profile --profile fa-cloudwatch-lab
cliSteps.explanation: Create the EC2 instance profile container.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response includes InstanceProfileName fa-cloudwatch-instance-profile.
cliSteps.warning: IAM is global; omit --region.

cliSteps.command: aws iam add-role-to-instance-profile --instance-profile-name fa-cloudwatch-instance-profile --role-name fa-cloudwatch-instance-role --profile fa-cloudwatch-lab
cliSteps.explanation: Associate the role with the instance profile that EC2 attaches at launch.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command completes without output.
cliSteps.warning: Wait briefly if EC2 does not immediately show the instance profile.

verification.title: Verify required role policies
verification.instruction: Open IAM > Roles > fa-cloudwatch-instance-role > Permissions.
verification.expectedResult: AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore and CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy are attached.

tasks.title: Launch the Amazon Linux instance with the unified CloudWatch Agent configuration
tasks.feature: Amazon EC2, Systems Manager, and CloudWatch Agent
tasks.goal: Launch fa-cloudwatch-instance with no inbound access, install the CloudWatch Agent, collect CPU, memory, disk, and application logs, and generate harmless sample events.
tasks.whyItMatters: Amazon EC2 publishes standard metrics such as CPUUtilization. Memory and filesystem metrics require the CloudWatch Agent. The agent also streams the local application log into CloudWatch Logs.

consoleSteps.title: Launch the monitored instance

instructions.text: Enter fa-cloudwatch-instance in Name and tags.
Under Key pair, choose Proceed without a key pair.
Set Auto-assign public IP to Enable.
Select fa-cloudwatch-instance-role in IAM instance profile.
Select Enable in Detailed CloudWatch monitoring.
Paste the displayed user-data script into User data.
Record Instance ID from the Instance ID column as [INSTANCE_ID].
Wait until Instance state is Running.
Wait until Status check is 2/2 checks passed.

jsonBlocks.title: fa-cloudwatch-instance user data script

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The instance starts with detailed EC2 monitoring, a running harmless app log generator, and a running CloudWatch Agent.
consoleSteps.warning: The user-data script intentionally writes synthetic INFO and ERROR text only. It contains no credentials, secrets, private keys, or personal data.

cliSteps.command: aws ssm get-parameter --name /aws/service/ami-amazon-linux-latest/al2023-ami-kernel-default-x86_64 --query Parameter.Value --output text --profile fa-cloudwatch-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record the returned AMI ID as [AL2023_AMI_ID]. The public Systems Manager parameter supplies a current Amazon Linux 2023 AMI ID for this Region.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns an ami- identifier.
cliSteps.warning: Use this x86_64 AMI ID only with a compatible instance type such as t3.micro.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 run-instances --image-id [AL2023_AMI_ID] --instance-type t3.micro --count 1 --subnet-id [SUBNET_ID] --security-group-ids [INSTANCE_SG_ID] --iam-instance-profile Name=fa-cloudwatch-instance-profile --monitoring Enabled=true --user-data file://fa-cloudwatch-instance-user-data.sh --tag-specifications ResourceType=instance,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-cloudwatch-instance}] --profile fa-cloudwatch-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Save the exact user-data script shown in this task as fa-cloudwatch-instance-user-data.sh. Record Instances[0].InstanceId as [INSTANCE_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains one pending instance with tag Name=fa-cloudwatch-instance.
cliSteps.warning: Detailed monitoring incurs charges. The instance security group contains no inbound rules.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 wait instance-status-ok --instance-ids [INSTANCE_ID] --profile fa-cloudwatch-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Wait until both EC2 system and instance checks report OK.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The waiter returns with no output.
cliSteps.warning: This does not prove that CloudWatch Agent metrics have arrived; perform the later telemetry verification.

verification.title: Verify Systems Manager management
verification.instruction: Open Systems Manager > Fleet Manager > Managed nodes and locate fa-cloudwatch-instance.
verification.expectedResult: The node appears as a managed node with Ping status Online.

verification.title: Verify local agent status
verification.instruction: Open Systems Manager > Session Manager > Start session, select fa-cloudwatch-instance, and run sudo /opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/bin/amazon-cloudwatch-agent-ctl -m ec2 -a status.
verification.expectedResult: The returned JSON reports status running.

tasks.title: Inspect EC2 standard metrics, agent custom metrics, logs, dimensions, periods, statistics, and percentiles
tasks.goal: View standard AWS/EC2 metrics and custom fa-cloudwatch/Agent metrics, then inspect the log stream and retention setting.
tasks.whyItMatters: A namespace groups metrics. A dimension identifies a particular time series. A period is the duration represented by one point. Statistics summarize values in each period, while percentile statistics help assess tail behavior.

consoleSteps.title: Inspect standard EC2 and custom agent metrics

instructions.text: Change Statistic from Average to p90.
Observe that the p90 line represents a high-end percentile rather than an average.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: CPUUtilization is visible under AWS/EC2 and memory/disk metrics are visible under fa-cloudwatch/Agent with an InstanceId dimension.
consoleSteps.warning: Percentiles require enough sample data to be meaningful. One small lab instance will not produce a production-like distribution.

consoleSteps.title: Inspect application logs and retention
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The log group contains harmless heartbeat and synthetic-error-for-training events, and its retention is 7 days.
consoleSteps.warning: CloudWatch Logs ingestion, storage, and Logs Insights scanning can incur charges. Keep the small retention period for this lab.

cliSteps.command: aws cloudwatch list-metrics --namespace AWS/EC2 --metric-name CPUUtilization --dimensions Name=InstanceId,Value=[INSTANCE_ID] --profile fa-cloudwatch-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: List the standard EC2 CPU metric series for the instance dimension.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response lists a CPUUtilization metric with Dimension Name InstanceId.
cliSteps.warning: Replace [INSTANCE_ID] with the ID recorded at launch.

cliSteps.command: aws cloudwatch list-metrics --namespace fa-cloudwatch/Agent --profile fa-cloudwatch-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: List CloudWatch Agent custom metrics such as mem_used_percent and disk_used_percent.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response lists agent metric names with an InstanceId dimension.
cliSteps.warning: Initial agent metrics can take several minutes to appear.

cliSteps.command: aws logs describe-log-groups --log-group-name-prefix /fa-cloudwatch/application --query logGroups[0].{Name:logGroupName,Retention:retentionInDays} --output table --profile fa-cloudwatch-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Verify the log group name and its seven-day retention policy.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The table shows /fa-cloudwatch/application and 7.
cliSteps.warning: The log group is created by the agent configuration at instance startup.

verification.title: Explain the metric terms
verification.instruction: State what namespace, dimension, period, statistic, and percentile mean for the metrics just viewed.
verification.expectedResult: Namespace groups metrics; InstanceId identifies the series; period is one minute; Average summarizes values; p90 shows a value below which roughly 90 percent of samples fall.

tasks.title: Create a metric filter and publish one direct custom metric
tasks.feature: CloudWatch Logs metric filters and custom metrics
tasks.goal: Convert synthetic ERROR log events into fa-cloudwatch/LogMetrics:ErrorCount and publish fa-cloudwatch/App:DemoRequests.
tasks.whyItMatters: A metric filter turns matching log events into a numerical CloudWatch metric that can be graphed or alarmed on. PutMetricData is appropriate when the application can publish a metric directly.

consoleSteps.title: Create the ERROR metric filter
consoleSteps.expectedResult: fa-cloudwatch-error-filter creates ErrorCount datapoints when the synthetic error text arrives.
consoleSteps.warning: Metric filters process new matching log events. Wait for the app service to emit another ERROR event after filter creation.

consoleSteps.title: Publish a direct custom metric through CloudShell
consoleSteps.instruction: Open the AWS Console top navigation bar.

instructions.text: Open the AWS Console top navigation bar.
Wait for the CloudShell prompt in eu-west-2.
Run the displayed AWS CLI command.

jsonBlocks.title: CloudShell command
jsonBlocks.content: aws cloudwatch put-metric-data --namespace fa-cloudwatch/App --metric-name DemoRequests --dimensions Environment=training --value 1 --unit Count --region eu-west-2

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The fa-cloudwatch/App namespace contains DemoRequests with Environment=training.
consoleSteps.warning: CloudShell uses the signed-in training user's permissions. A CloudWatch metric has no immediate delete API; it becomes inactive after publishing stops and later expires according to CloudWatch metric retention.

cliSteps.command: aws logs put-metric-filter --log-group-name /fa-cloudwatch/application --filter-name fa-cloudwatch-error-filter --filter-pattern synthetic-error-for-training --metric-transformations metricName=ErrorCount,metricNamespace=fa-cloudwatch/LogMetrics,metricValue=1 --profile fa-cloudwatch-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Create the metric filter that maps each matching future log event to an ErrorCount value of 1.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command completes without output.
cliSteps.warning: Wait for a subsequent synthetic error event before expecting metric data.

cliSteps.command: aws cloudwatch put-metric-data --namespace fa-cloudwatch/App --metric-name DemoRequests --dimensions Environment=training --value 1 --unit Count --profile fa-cloudwatch-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Publish one harmless custom metric point directly to CloudWatch.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command completes without output.
cliSteps.warning: Custom metrics can incur charges. Publish only this single training datapoint.

verification.title: Verify log-derived metric data
verification.instruction: Open CloudWatch > Metrics > Custom namespaces > fa-cloudwatch/LogMetrics after at least one new ERROR event arrives.
verification.expectedResult: ErrorCount is available.

verification.title: Verify direct custom metric data
verification.instruction: Open CloudWatch > Metrics > Custom namespaces > fa-cloudwatch/App.
verification.expectedResult: DemoRequests is available with Environment=training.

tasks.title: Create SNS notifications and confirm the email subscription
tasks.goal: Create fa-cloudwatch-alerts and one learner-confirmed email subscription before creating notification alarms.
tasks.whyItMatters: CloudWatch alarms can notify an SNS topic when their state changes. Email subscriptions remain Pending confirmation until the recipient confirms the message.

consoleSteps.title: Create and confirm the SNS subscription

instructions.text: Enter an email inbox you control in Endpoint.
Open the AWS Notification - Subscription Confirmation message.
Record the Subscription ARN displayed for the confirmed subscription as [SNS_SUBSCRIPTION_ARN].

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The subscription Status is Confirmed instead of PendingConfirmation.
consoleSteps.warning: The email address is learner-specific. AWS sends a confirmation message; alarms cannot deliver to an unconfirmed email subscription.

cliSteps.command: aws sns create-topic --name fa-cloudwatch-alerts --profile fa-cloudwatch-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record the returned TopicArn as [SNS_TOPIC_ARN].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains an ARN ending in :fa-cloudwatch-alerts.
cliSteps.warning: Use only this training topic for the lab.

cliSteps.command: aws sns subscribe --topic-arn [SNS_TOPIC_ARN] --protocol email --notification-endpoint <EMAIL_INBOX_YOU_CONTROL> --profile fa-cloudwatch-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Replace <EMAIL_INBOX_YOU_CONTROL> with an email address that you can open. Record SubscriptionArn if it is returned; it remains pending until the inbox confirmation link is selected.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response initially reports SubscriptionArn as pending confirmation.
cliSteps.warning: Never use another person's email address without permission.

verification.title: Verify confirmation
verification.instruction: In SNS > Topics > fa-cloudwatch-alerts > Subscriptions, inspect the subscription status.

tasks.title: Create a static alarm and an anomaly-detection alarm, then test states safely
tasks.goal: Create an ErrorCount static alarm and a CPU anomaly-detection alarm with SNS notifications, then use SetAlarmState for a controlled notification test.
tasks.whyItMatters: An alarm starts in INSUFFICIENT_DATA until it has enough data. It is OK when the evaluated metric does not breach the condition and ALARM when it does. Static thresholds suit known limits; anomaly detection suits changing baselines.

consoleSteps.title: Create the static ErrorCount alarm
consoleSteps.expectedResult: fa-cloudwatch-error-alarm evaluates ErrorCount and notifies fa-cloudwatch-alerts when one or more matching errors occur in a minute.
consoleSteps.warning: The synthetic app intentionally emits an error every minute, so this alarm can enter ALARM during the lab.

consoleSteps.title: Create the CPU anomaly-detection alarm

instructions.text: Set the evaluation period to 1 minute.
Wait for CloudWatch to collect baseline data.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: fa-cloudwatch-cpu-anomaly-alarm is created using an anomaly-detection band for the selected CPU metric.
consoleSteps.warning: Anomaly detection needs historical behavior. The small lab may remain INSUFFICIENT_DATA or not enter ALARM; this is normal.

consoleSteps.title: Perform a controlled alarm notification test

instructions.text: Enter controlled training notification test in State reason.
Enter controlled training reset in State reason.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The alarm history records the manual ALARM and OK state changes, and the confirmed inbox receives the alarm notification.
consoleSteps.warning: Set state is a controlled testing action. Do not use it to mask real production alarms.

cliSteps.command: aws cloudwatch put-metric-alarm --alarm-name fa-cloudwatch-error-alarm --alarm-description "Training alarm for synthetic application errors" --namespace fa-cloudwatch/LogMetrics --metric-name ErrorCount --statistic Sum --period 60 --evaluation-periods 1 --threshold 1 --comparison-operator GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold --alarm-actions [SNS_TOPIC_ARN] --treat-missing-data notBreaching --profile fa-cloudwatch-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Create the static alarm. Replace [SNS_TOPIC_ARN] with the ARN returned by create-topic.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command completes without output; a new metric alarm initially commonly shows INSUFFICIENT_DATA.
cliSteps.warning: Creating an alarm can cause CloudWatch service-linked roles to be created automatically when AWS requires them.

cliSteps.command: aws cloudwatch put-metric-alarm --alarm-name fa-cloudwatch-cpu-anomaly-alarm --alarm-description "Training CPU anomaly alarm" --comparison-operator GreaterThanUpperThreshold --evaluation-periods 1 --metrics file://fa-cloudwatch-cpu-anomaly-metrics.json --alarm-actions [SNS_TOPIC_ARN] --profile fa-cloudwatch-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Save the exact metrics array below as fa-cloudwatch-cpu-anomaly-metrics.json and replace [INSTANCE_ID] and [SNS_TOPIC_ARN] before running. This command creates the anomaly detector as part of creating the anomaly alarm.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command completes without output.
cliSteps.warning: Anomaly alarms cannot have Auto Scaling actions.

cliSteps.command: aws cloudwatch set-alarm-state --alarm-name fa-cloudwatch-error-alarm --state-value ALARM --state-reason "controlled training notification test" --profile fa-cloudwatch-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Force a temporary ALARM state to validate the confirmed email path without changing application infrastructure.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command completes without output and the SNS topic receives an ALARM notification.
cliSteps.warning: Immediately run the next reset command after checking the notification.

cliSteps.command: aws cloudwatch set-alarm-state --alarm-name fa-cloudwatch-error-alarm --state-value OK --state-reason "controlled training reset" --profile fa-cloudwatch-lab --region eu-west-2

cliSteps.expectedResult: The command completes without output and alarm history records the change.

tasks.goal: Create one composite alarm that notifies only when both underlying alarms are ALARM.

tasks.goal: Create fa-cloudwatch-dashboard with metric and log widgets, then run complete Logs Insights queries.

jsonBlocks.title: Dashboard log-widget query
jsonBlocks.content: SOURCE '/fa-cloudwatch/application' | fields @timestamp, @message | filter @message like /synthetic-error-for-training/ | sort @timestamp desc | limit 20

consoleSteps.title: Run complete Logs Insights queries

instructions.text: Set the time range to Last 1 hour.
Replace the query with the counts-by-level query.

jsonBlocks.title: Recent-error query
jsonBlocks.content:
fields @timestamp, @message, @logStream
| filter @message like /synthetic-error-for-training/
| sort @timestamp desc
| limit 20

jsonBlocks.title: Counts-by-level query
jsonBlocks.content:
fields @timestamp, @message
| parse @message /level=(?<level>\w+)/
| stats count(*) as events by level
| sort events desc
